notes: **Three things hold the number down, and all three can be changed.** First, earnings after a market wage are thin: buyers pay for what is left after someone else is paid to do the owner's work, and that is about $170,000, not the $585,000 the books show before the owner is paid. Second, the owner personally produces 76.8% of charges and holds the facility relationships, so most of the goodwill would leave with the owner unless the owner stays on under contract. Third, the billing patterns in the risk review (complex care management volume, visit levels, place of service) would be found in any buyer's diligence and would be priced as a discount, an escrow or a reason to walk away. **What moves it up:** every additional $100,000 of sustainable earnings is worth roughly $300,000 at this multiple. A clean outside coding audit, a second and third clinician carrying the census, written facility agreements, monthly accrual-basis statements and two years of growth are what move a buyer from 3 times earnings toward 4 or 5. As an illustration only: revenue of $1.4 million with $330,000 of normalized earnings at 4 to 5 times would be worth about $1.3 to $1.6 million. **What moves it down:** if care-management billing cannot be supported and stops, earnings fall by up to the amount it collects and past payments may have to be returned. That is the low case.

inputs: Reported sales of small primary care practices (revenue under $5 million): 3 to 6 times EBITDA (Scope Research, 2025). Taken down one turn for a single physician, government fee-for-service payers and facility relationships the practice does not own.
5 to 6 times (about $850,000 to $1,020,000) needs a strategic buyer in post-acute or senior care, the owner staying for several years, and documented, transferable relationships.
notes: The method a medical group, health system or investor-backed platform would use. It pays for earnings that remain after every clinician, including the owner, is paid a market wage.

inputs: Medical practices sold through a national business marketplace, 2021 to 2025: median 2.05 times owner earnings, middle half 1.46 to 2.94 (BizBuySell data quoted by Iconic, 2026). The lower half of that range is used because one physician produces most of the earnings.
notes: The method an individual physician buying the practice to run it would use. It gives the highest answer because the buyer is also buying a job. Few physicians buy facility-based practices this way, so it carries a quarter of the weight.
